items.title: Does the LDS Church Lie About Its History? ExMormon LEGEND Wendy Jensen Answers the Question
items.summary: A Mormon News Roundup YouTube video featuring Wendy Jensen on whether the LDS Church lies about its own history or makes the difficult parts of that history hard for ordinary members to find.

items.title: ‘Secret Lives of Mormon Wives’ star Dakota Mortensen files defamation lawsuit against Hulu
items.summary: The Salt Lake Tribune reports that Dakota Mortensen, a star of Hulu's ‘Secret Lives of Mormon Wives,’ filed a defamation lawsuit against Hulu. He alleges the show spread "statements of fact that were fabricated."

items.title: Ep366: Inside Wade Christofferson's Sentencing: Courtroom Observer Weighs In
items.summary: On Mormonish, a courtroom observer who attended Wade Christofferson's sentencing shares what they saw and heard as the prosecutor, family members and victim advocates spoke. The episode notes he was sentenced to 45 years in federal prison.

items.title: What is doctrine?
items.summary: A Wheat & Tares blog post says its author has seen "three different working definitions" of doctrine used in practice.

items.title: 96MW data center planned on rural Texas ranch owned by Mormon Church
items.summary: Data Center Dynamics reports that Aetheris Infrastructure has been granted permission to build a 96MW data center and a 180MW natural gas power plant on 4,252 acres of the Triangle Ranch in Cottle County, Texas, most of it owned by the church through its FarmlandReserve subsidiary. The site reports FarmlandReserve said leasing portions of its properties for commercial uses fits its long-term investment strategy.

items.title: Dr. Gregory Prince: The Mormon Faith Crisis and the Church's Crisis of Trust
items.summary: In this Mormon Discussion episode, host Bill Reel interviews historian Gregory Prince about what happens when a church's efforts to protect faith end up damaging trust. The video is a commentary-style interview.

items.title: 'Mormon Land': How this LDS election leader found the courage to stand up to Trump — and win
items.summary: On The Salt Lake Tribune's Mormon Land podcast, Utah Lt. Gov. Deidre Henderson, a Latter-day Saint who refused a Justice Department demand for Utah's complete voter rolls, talks about her faith, political convictions and the midterm elections.
